text.p: The following are leading domestic stories in Portuguese newspapers.
- The Government has presented a calendar for privatisations for 1998-99 which would earn 800 billion escudos.
- The Finance Ministry is launching a programme to calculate debts owed by individual taxpayers, linked to the amount of the debts and the extent of the delay in repaying them.
- The National Institute of Agricultural Garantees will freeze payments of subsidies to farmers who have made false declarations about the size of their cultivated areas.

- Financial concessions given by the Portuguese government to a private firm for the construction of a new bridge in Lisbon, the so-called Vasco da Gama bridge, will have no effect on its 1997 budget deficit, the European Union has said.

- The Portuguese government will reduce to a minimum its stakes in companies, according to the privatisation plan for 1998/99. The revenues from privatisations will help Portugal cut its public debt to 59.4 percent of GDP in 2000.

- Marco Maciel, Brazil's Vice-President, said economic ties between Portugal and Brazil are improving and that the investment of Portuguese companies in Brazil, and Brazilian companies in Portugal, is increasing.
- Court cases involving debts by families doubled between 1990 and 1995. Younger people are the most indebted.
- 3,000 new industrial companies created in Portugal in 1996. Despite the growing importance of the services sector, new industrial companies are opening at a brisk pace.
